Projects

Featured · Undergraduate thesis · 2024–2025

Arduino-Based Smart City Lighting System (ASCLS)

Arduino UnoESP8266LDR + IR sensorsThingSpeakTinkerCAD

An IoT-enabled adaptive street-lighting prototype. Conventional streetlights burn at full power all night, whatever the traffic. ASCLS dims lights when streets are empty and brightens them the moment someone approaches, while streaming live data to the cloud so a city could monitor performance remotely. Supervised by Roheen Qamar; I led the research with a team of four and wrote the full manuscript, published as a ResearchGate preprint (2025).

For people & planet: Streets that stay safe without wasting power. Lighting is a large share of what cities spend on electricity, and many communities can't afford to waste it. ASCLS shows a low-cost way to light only what is needed: protecting people on the road while cutting energy use and emissions.

ConditionLDR (light)IR (motion)Streetlight
DayHighn/aOff
Night, no motionLowNoneDim
Night, motionLowDetectedBright

What I did

  • Designed rule-based control logic with PWM brightness (off / dim / bright)
  • Added ESP8266 Wi-Fi connectivity sending live readings to ThingSpeak
  • Simulated and validated the circuit in TinkerCAD before building
  • Tested three scenarios: daytime, night without motion, night with motion
  • Reviewed 30+ papers on sensor-based automation and smart lighting

What I learned & what's next

  • Limits found: Wi-Fi instability, IR false positives, single-lamp scale
  • Next: ML-based predictive lighting, multi-node networks, solar and battery backup, ESP32/NodeMCU for reliability
  • Why it matters: lighting is a large share of public electricity use, so even small efficiency gains scale
Database project · Database Administration & Management

Library Management System

MySQLER modellingRole-based accessSolo project

A relational database design for a university library that tracks books, individual copies, issues and returns, and overdue fines, with different rules for students and faculty. Course project for Dr. Muniba Memon.

For people & planet: Fair, organised access to knowledge. Clear borrowing limits, honest records and a transparent fine system keep shared resources available to everyone who needs them.

Design highlights

  • Separate Users, Books and Issued Books tables linked by keys
  • A Limits by Role table sets how many books and days students and faculty get
  • Issue records track issue, due and return dates
  • A Fines table links each fine to the issue that caused it

Implementation & security

  • Built and populated in MySQL (phpMyAdmin) with sample users, books and loans
  • Four roles: Admin (full access), Librarian (create/read/update), Student and Faculty (read-only on books and their own records)
  • Designed for data integrity and accountability
Front-end project

Tic Tac Toe

HTMLCSSJavaScript

A small browser game with a soft pastel interface, rounded tiles, and clear controls: New Game to keep playing and Reset Game to start from scratch. It announces the winner, or a draw, when a round ends. It was an exercise in turning game logic into clean, friendly interaction, practising DOM events, state handling and responsive layout.

For people & planet: Technology that feels welcoming. A friendly, easy interface that anyone can pick up in seconds. It taught me that good design lowers the barrier to using technology.

Visual design · Branding & social media

The Daily Grind

Brand identitySocial contentVisual storytelling

A campaign concept for a neighbourhood café that doubles as a study space. I developed a warm, crafted look (kraft paper, hand-lettered type, a rabbit-barista emblem) and a set of Instagram-style posts that tell the café's story.

For people & planet: Design that gives back to a community. The brand puts student affordability and local artists at the centre, so a café becomes a space that supports the people around it.

Content system

  • Logo emblem and consistent paper-and-coffee palette
  • "Meet the team" character posts for the owner and barista
  • Organic sandwich menu graphic with playful item names
  • New-item launch and "perfect afternoon duo" engagement posts
  • A feed mockup showing how the content appears to customers

Community-minded ideas

  • "10 AM Fuel": 10% off for university students during quieter study hours
  • Rotating gallery walls to showcase and sell local student and emerging artists' work
  • Shows how design can carry values, not just visuals
